lead: The Great Fast reaches its midpoint today, and the readings ask what we are choosing. Abram lets his nephew choose first, and Lot goes by what looks good to his eyes. In John, many disciples walk away from a hard teaching, and Peter answers for those who stay. Between these stand the capture of Ai in the second reading, a hard page of ancient war to be read in the light of Christ, and Paul’s word that salvation is for all who call on the Lord. At the middle of the road the question is simple: to whom shall we go?

set: Abram has come back from Egypt rich, and Lot has flocks of his own. The land cannot support them both, and their herders quarrel (13:5–7). The chapter says that the Canaanites and Perizzites were then living in the land, so this family quarrel takes place in full view of the neighbours.
The “Plain” is the region of the lower Jordan, which looks green from the hills near Bethel. The narrator adds a warning: all this was before Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed.
str: vv. 8–9: Abram’s proposal, and the choice given to Lot.
vv. 10–13: Lot looks, chooses and moves toward Sodom.
vv. 14–17: God tells Abram to look, and renews the promise.
v. 18: Abram moves to Mamre and builds an altar.
kw: A quarrel, sometimes a case at law. Exodus 17:7 uses the same word as a place name, Meribah, where the people quarrelled with God.
Literally “brothers”, though Lot is Abram’s nephew. Hebrew uses this word for close relatives. Abram’s argument is short: we are family.
The great trees near Hebron where Abraham will later receive three visitors (Genesis 18:1). Abram’s new home will be the place of that visit.
vv: Is not the whole land before you?
Abram is the elder and the one who received the promise, and he could have chosen first. He gives up that right because he knows that the land is God’s to give.
Lot looked about him, and saw that the plain of the Jordan was well watered everywhere like the garden of the Lord,

The words recall Eden, but the next phrase names Sodom. What looks like paradise may be the road to ruin. Lot does not sin in choosing, but he chooses only by what he sees, and soon he has moved “as far as Sodom” (v. 12).
Raise your eyes now, and look from the place where you are,
Lot raised his eyes for himself. Abram, having given way, is told by God to raise his. The one who let go of the choice is given more than he could have chosen.
ch: St John Chrysostom, preaching on Genesis, admires the humility of the elder who gives the choice to the younger (in substance). The passage prepares for the Lord’s word, “Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth” (Matthew 5:5), and “Blessed are the peacemakers” (Matthew 5:9). The Catechism teaches that respect for persons and for the bonds between them belongs to the peace that the fifth commandment protects (CCC 2304).

set: Jesus has fed the five thousand and taught in the synagogue at Capernaum (6:59) that he is the bread of life: “the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh” (6:51), and “my flesh is true food” (6:55). The earlier listeners in the chapter were the crowd. Now it is his own disciples who find this too hard. John does not narrate the institution of the Eucharist at the Last Supper; this chapter does that work, and this is how it ends.
str: vv. 62–65: Jesus answers: the Son of Man’s ascent, spirit and flesh, the Father’s gift.
vv. 67–69: the question to the Twelve, and Peter’s confession.
kw: Literally “hard”, like dry, rough ground. The word here means not that the teaching is hard to understand but that it is hard to accept.
To make someone stumble, from skandalon, a stumbling block.
Peter’s title for Jesus. The only other place the Gospels use it is on the lips of a demon (Mark 1:24; Luke 4:34). It names the one set apart by God and belonging wholly to him.
vv: It is the spirit that gives life; the flesh is useless.

This does not take back what Jesus has said about his flesh. “Flesh” here is human nature left to itself: human reasoning alone cannot receive this teaching. The Malayalam POC has “body” at this point. St Augustine explains that the flesh would be of no use if it were understood as meat sold in a market, but joined to the Spirit it gives life (Tractates on John 27; in substance).
Because of this many of his disciples turned back and no longer went about with him.
Jesus does not run after them to soften his words. The reason John gives for their leaving is the teaching about the bread of life.
Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.
Peter does not say that he understands. He says that there is nowhere else to go. Sometimes that is what faith looks like at the midpoint of the road, and he says “we”, speaking for the Twelve.
ch: The Catechism quotes this passage directly: the first announcement of the Eucharist divided the disciples, just as the announcement of the Passion scandalized them; the Eucharist and the Cross are stumbling blocks, and the Lord’s question, “Do you also wish to go away?”, sounds through the ages as an invitation to discover that only he has the words of eternal life (CCC 1336). Every reception of Holy Qurbana is an answer to it.

qa: Does “the flesh is useless” mean that the Eucharist is only a symbol?

No. Jesus has just said “my flesh is true food” (6:55), and the disciples leave because they understood him to mean it. Verse 63 contrasts “flesh”, human nature on its own, with the Spirit who gives life. The Church believes that Christ is truly, really and substantially present in the Eucharist (CCC 1374), and only the Spirit opens us to this faith.
rite: The midpoint of the Great Fast is marked in the calendar of the Syro-Malabar Church, and in some parishes the Cross is honoured today with special prayers, according to local custom. Today’s Gospel fits the day: halfway along the road, the Lord asks those who remain whether they too wish to go.
study: Where in my family or parish could I, like Abram, give up the first choice for the sake of peace?
Which teaching of Christ do I find hard? What would it mean to say, with Peter, “to whom can we go?”
